THE DIRECTIONS

You will talk to four people. Record what you would say to each one. You can record again as many times as you want. When all four are recorded, click Submit.

The first time you press record, your computer will ask to use your microphone. Click Allow.

The tower scorecard

As you record, the four scores fill in. Multiply STAYS UP by 3, add LOW COST, and compare the towers.

THE SCENE

You made it to the last room of the school puzzle game. The last puzzle asks you to pick your team's best model tower. Tower A has a pole in the center. Tower B does not. Both towers were tested on a table that shakes like an earthquake. You need four scores to choose. Four people each can help you.

THE HISTORY

This puzzle game is about pagodas, the tall wooden towers of Japan. Japan has many earthquakes, but old pagodas almost never fall. One in Nara has stood for 1,300 years. Each has one tall pole standing in its center.
